title: Template Method and State
idea: Template Method fixes an algorithm's step order in a base class while subclasses fill the varying steps. State gives each status its own class that handles actions.

analogy.text: A chain of bakeries follows one fixed recipe order, but each branch picks its own filling. A ticket gate's button opens it only after you pay.
analogy.breaks: Branches may reorder steps; `final` forbids that. Gates are wired; Java states are swapped.

points: Template Method: a `final` base method calls abstract steps in a fixed order.
Subclasses fill abstract steps and may override hooks, methods with a default body.
State: the context holds a current state object and forwards every action to it.
Each state class answers the actions it allows and returns the next state.

hero.title: An order's life as state objects

steps.caption: A new `Order` holds a `Created` object in its `state` field.
`ship()` is forwarded to `Created`. It has no `ship` override, so the default returns itself: refused.
`pay()` is forwarded to `Created`, which returns a new `Paid`. The order swaps its state.
`Cancelled` overrides nothing, so every later action is refused. No `if` checks a status.
A new status reached by existing actions is one new class plus the overrides that lead to it. `Order` keeps no status `if`.

code.title: Template Method
code.caption: One fixed export routine, two formats. Subclasses fill the steps, never the order.

walk.text: `export` is the template method. `final` stops subclasses from reordering its steps.
Abstract steps: every subclass must supply a header and a row format.
A hook: an empty default that subclasses may override if they need it.
`CsvExport` fills the two required steps and skips the hook.
`JsonExport` also overrides the hook to close the array.
`main` calls the same `export` on both; the base class drives the flow.

code.title: State
code.caption: Each status is a class. `Order` forwards actions and swaps to whatever state comes back.

walk.text: The state contract. Defaults return `this`, so a disallowed action is a no-op.
Each state overrides only the actions it allows and returns the next state.
Final states override nothing: every action is refused.
`Order` is the context. It has no status `switch`; it delegates.
`move` reports the transition and stores the next state.
`main` tries a mix of allowed and refused actions.

pitfalls: Do not use Template Method when steps vary independently; pass Strategy objects instead.
Mark the template method `final`, or a subclass can override it and skip steps.
Skip State for two statuses and one rule; an `enum` and a `switch` read better.

quiz.q: What is the fourth line `StateDemo` prints?
quiz.why: The third call moved the order to `Cancelled`. It overrides no action, so `pay` falls to the default, which returns the same state.

takeaway: Template Method fixes the steps; State swaps the object that answers actions.
